{"type":"text","timestamp":1794624333711,"sessionID":"ses_e280fdd14ffepmMjK2QgqKzF8T","part":{"id":"prt_1d7f22785001OuWTorYVaeg0eq","messageID":"msg_1d7f20632001snqIeq9wIahxg6","sessionID":"ses_e280fdd14ffepmMjK2QgqKzF8T","type":"text","text":"The episode is over and the mission failed: the battery ran out at about tick 48 of 50, so the score is 0.\n\n**What went right:** the rover sampled all six targets, including the one that appeared mid-mission (d1).\n- **On time:** t2 (worth 2), t4 (2), t5 (1) and t1 (1).\n- **Late, at a quarter of full value:** t3 (0.25 instead of 1). My first sample attempt missed by about 1 m because of heading drift, and the retry came after its deadline.\n- **Late:** d1 (0.75 instead of 3). By the time I learned about it, my queued commands committed the rover to t1 first, and d1 was 16.5 m away.\n\n**What went wrong:** I never budgeted the battery. Every tick costs 0.5 even when idle, which adds up to 25 over the 50 ticks, and that ate the margin. When I finally did the sums at tick 28, the battery was already short: the commands I had queued (the drive to t1, the drive to d1 and two samples) plus the remaining idle drain came to about 1.2 more than was left. That was before counting any drive back to base. Queued commands can't be cancelled; only hitting a hazard or the map edge clears the queue, and neither was on the route. So from that point the loss was locked in. The telemetry confirms it: 6.77 left after the d1 sample at tick 34, and 0.27 at tick 47.\n\nThe plan needed about 10 more battery than it had. I should have kept a running total of the battery from the start and dropped the low-value targets: t3 was already late, and t1 was worth only 1. That would have left enough for d1 and the drive home.","time":{"start":1794624333701,"end":1794624333709}}}
